the niffler raiding the bank for anything shiny

Crisp golden choux puffs made with gruyère and a pinch of cayenne, baked until hollow and shiny, piled up like a niffler's stash. Bring 125ml water, 125ml milk, 100g butter and a pinch of salt to the boil. Tip in 150g plain flour and beat over the heat for 2 minutes until the dough leaves the sides. Cool 5 minutes, then beat in 4 eggs one at a time until glossy. Stir in 120g grated gruyère and a pinch of cayenne. Pipe walnut-size balls onto lined trays, top with a little more cheese and bake at 200C for 20 to 25 minutes until golden and hollow.
M: the Goldstein sisters' apartment in New York

Beef chuck browned and braised at 160C for 3 hours with onion, carrot and stock, potatoes added for the last hour. Season a 1.5kg beef chuck roast and brown all over in a heavy pot. Add 2 quartered onions, 3 carrots in chunks, 2 garlic cloves, 2 thyme sprigs, 1 tbsp tomato paste and 500ml beef stock. Cover and braise at 160C for 2 hours. Add 800g halved potatoes and cook 1 hour more until everything is tender. Lift out the beef and veg, simmer the juices to thicken slightly and pour over the sliced meat.

s.note: Puff pastry cut into animal shapes and baked with cinnamon sugar
s.how: Cut 2 sheets of puff pastry into little animal shapes with cutters or a knife. Brush with beaten egg and sprinkle generously with cinnamon sugar. Bake at 200C for 12 minutes until puffed and golden. Cool on a rack and arrange like a bakery window.

s.note: Boiled eggs with a Dijon mayo yolk filling, dusted with smoked paprika
s.how: Boil 8 eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel. Halve and mash the yolks with mayonnaise and Dijon until smooth, then pipe back into the whites and dust with smoked paprika. Set out on the bar beside a bowl of green olives.

m.note: Potato and cheddar dumplings, boiled then fried in butter
m.how: Boil and mash 600g potatoes, then mix with 150g grated cheddar. Fill dumpling wrappers and pinch closed. Boil for 3 minutes until they float, drain, then fry in butter with sliced onion until golden on both sides. Serve with sour cream.

w.note: Filo rolled around cinnamon green apple and sultanas
w.how: Toss 4 sliced green apples with 80g sultanas, a teaspoon of cinnamon, sugar and a handful of breadcrumbs. Layer buttered filo sheets, spread the filling along one edge and roll up. Brush with butter and bake at 190C for 35 minutes. Dust with icing sugar.

d.note: Fresh lemon juice and sugar syrup over ice, topped with soda water
d.how: Dissolve 100g sugar in a little hot water and cool. Squeeze 6 lemons into a jug, add the syrup, plenty of ice and top with cold soda water. Pour into teacups so it looks innocent, adding a splash of gin to the cups for the grown-ups.
